item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Pica Code IR-2026-115 - Identification and functional characterization of extracellular vesicles involved in the pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s Disease: focus on miRNAs as inflammatory modulators and biomarkers (Univ. MODENA e R. E.)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-27 13:00
Institution: Univ. MODENA e R. E., Modena
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The project aims to investigate the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in neuron–microglia communication during the early stages of Alzheimer’s disease. The candidate will isolate EVs from mouse brain tissue and assess their effects on primary neural and glial cultures. The cultures will be examined using immunofluorescence, mitochondrial activity assays, and western blotting. EVs will also be administered to healthy animals to investigate their effects on neuroinflammation in vivo. Specifically, microglial and astrocytic activation will be assessed by immunofluorescence, while inflammatory marker expression will be evaluated using western blotting and cytokine assays.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Modulation of the Kynurenine Pathway and Neurotransmitter Systems in the Kmo+/− Mouse Model Following Chronic Exposure to Cannabinoids (Univ. FERRARA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 12:00
Institution: Univ. FERRARA, Ferrara
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-11 Farmacologia

The project aims to characterize the effects of chronic exposure to THC and synthetic cannabinoids in the Kmo+/− mouse model. Potential alterations in the kynurenine pathway and different neurotransmitter systems will be assessed by HPLC analysis in selected brain regions. Neurochemical changes will be correlated with behavioral outcomes using specific behavioral tests. Biochemical and molecular analyses will complement the study to further elucidate the mechanisms underlying the response to cannabinoids.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: 2026-IdrDip-05-medmol - Nuclear Signalling Compartmentalization in Skeletal Muscle Aging: the Role of Kinase/Phosphatase Imbalance (Univ. PAVIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-25 12:00
Institution: Univ. PAVIA, Pavia
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

This project proposes the novel idea that the balance between nuclear kinases and phosphatases is crucial for skeletal muscle homeostasis during aging. To test this hypothesis, the candidate will use different techniques and novel tools (e.g., pooled optical CRISPR -FRET screenings, nuclear-targeted biosensors, spatial proteomics of nuclei in single fibers). The identification of new targets involved in age-related nuclear dysfunction and the conceptual idea that reframes sarcopenia as a nuclear signalling disorder, will be important to advance the knowledge in the field of aging.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Investigating the Muscle-specific Power of thyroid hormone to ACTivate body metabolism (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 12:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The assignment is aimed at collaborating on the experimental activities envisaged by the IMPACT project, using genetically modified mouse models and primary cultures of muscle stem cells. Activities will include the characterization of the muscle phenotype under physiological and pathological conditions, the analysis of metabolic parameters and energy homeostasis, as well as the study of alterations associated with muscle atrophy. Molecular and cellular biology methodologies will also be used to evaluate metabolic adaptations and gene expression in response to the modulation of thyroid hormone action.
